CHIEF COMPLAINT
Breast reduction consultation

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. The patient has been considering this procedure for approximately 6-7 years. She reports a long history of symptoms including back pain, neck pain, and shoulder discomfort since high school, which has worsened over time, particularly when working at a desk all day. She has been seeing a chiropractor for several years with minimal relief. She experiences bra strap indentations on her shoulders and occasionally reports numbness and tingling in her hands. The patient reports significant activity limitations with exercise, jumping, and running due to breast size and associated pain. She notes her breasts are always sweaty but denies rashes underneath. Currently wears a 34E sports bra as it is more comfortable and affordable than regular bras in her size. She has never had a prior consultation for breast reduction. The patient has recently lost 10 pounds and plans to lose an additional 20 pounds. She denies current children but may plan to have children in the future.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for back pain, neck pain, shoulder indentations, occasional numbness and tingling in hands, activity limitation, and excessive sweating under breasts. Denies rashes, nipple pain, or nipple discharge. Otherwise healthy.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chiropractic treatment for back pain for several years

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol for migraine management

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40. Patient counseled that screening mammograms are recommended starting at age 30.

SOCIAL HISTORY
College student currently studying psychology. Drinks wine occasionally. Denies tobacco and drug use. Currently transitioning to new health insurance plan through husband's employer, expected to take effect in July 2027.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Breasts: Asymmetrical with severe bilateral ptosis. One breast positioned slightly lower than the other. No nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or palpable axillary lymphadenopathy.

RESULTS
Body surface area: 2.65 m²
Schnur scale minimum required resection: 1,792 grams
Estimated post-operative breast size: Small C cup (B cup possible depending on blood supply preservation)
Potential for nipple graft given extent of reduction needed

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for evaluation of bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Patient is an excellent surgical candidate. Attempted nonsurgical management with chiropractic care has provided minimal relief. Plan for bilateral reduction mammoplasty using anchor incision technique with nipple repositioning and removal of excess fat and gland tissue. Anticipated resection volume of approximately 1,792 grams is attainable based on BSA and Schnur scale. Surgical time approximately 3 hours. Bilateral drains to be placed for approximately 1 week. Clear plastic tape to be applied over incisions. Patient to remain hospitalized overnight for pain control and monitoring. Expected post-operative restrictions include no heavy lifting and no driving for 2-3 weeks; activity restrictions for 6 weeks total. Patient counseled that approximately 30% of patients may not be able to breastfeed after procedure due to removal of glandular tissue. Informed of potential for altered or absent nipple sensation, though nipple sensation typically remains intact. Advised that breasts will change with weight gain, pregnancy, and aging. Defer insurance authorization submission until patient's new insurance plan becomes effective in July 2027. Photography to be obtained today for insurance documentation. Schedule follow-up appointment prior to surgery for final preoperative questions and detailed surgical instructions. Patient to contact office once new insurance information is available.
